title: CTS Church Growth — Unit 12: Retention: Closing the Back Door

blocks.en: 📈 Church Growth — Unit 12: Retention: Closing the Back Door
blocks.es_reference: 📈 Crecimiento de la Iglesia — Unidad 12: Retención: Cerrando la Puerta de Atrás

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Of those whom You gave Me I have lost none." — John 18:9 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "De los que me diste, no perdí ninguno." — Juan 18:9 (RVG)

blocks.en: By and large I have found it easier to retain members than to win new ones. I once knew a church that poured enormous effort into growth; over the years they recorded a long string of baptisms — and their attendance stayed about the same. Year after year they filled the front door and never noticed the open one in the back. That is the picture to keep before you in this final unit: it does no good to pour water into a bucket that leaks. The work of growth is only half done at the front door. The other half is closing the back.
blocks.es_reference: En general he hallado más fácil retener miembros que ganar nuevos. Una vez conocí una iglesia que volcó un esfuerzo enorme en el crecimiento; con los años registró una larga serie de bautismos — y su asistencia se mantuvo más o menos igual. Año tras año llenaban la puerta de entrada y nunca notaban la abierta en la parte de atrás. Esa es la imagen que hay que tener delante en esta unidad final: de nada sirve verter agua en un balde que gotea. La obra del crecimiento está solo a medio hacer en la puerta de entrada. La otra mitad es cerrar la de atrás.

blocks.en: When people drop out. People are most likely to slip away at four predictable seasons, and a wise church watches for them:
blocks.es_reference: Cuando la gente deserta. La gente tiende más a deslizarse en cuatro temporadas predecibles, y una iglesia sabia las vigila:

blocks.en: In the teen years, roughly fifteen to twenty-three — by far the highest dropout window. Most teenage dropouts do return later in life, especially in their late twenties and thirties, and the return is highest among those for whom faith was real in childhood. But the leak is real, and it is large.
blocks.es_reference: En los años de la adolescencia, más o menos de quince a veintitrés — por mucho la ventana de deserción más alta. La mayoría de los desertores adolescentes sí regresan más tarde en la vida, especialmente al final de sus veinte y en sus treinta, y el regreso es más alto entre aquellos para quienes la fe fue real en la niñez. Pero la fuga es real, y es grande.

blocks.en: In the first two years in a new community — when the old ties are cut and the new ones not yet formed.
blocks.es_reference: En los primeros dos años en una nueva comunidad — cuando los viejos lazos se cortan y los nuevos aún no se forman.

blocks.en: In the first years after the youngest child leaves home — when the family reason for attending walks out the door.
blocks.es_reference: En los primeros años después de que el hijo menor deja el hogar — cuando la razón familiar para asistir sale por la puerta.

blocks.en: Just after a divorce — when life fractures and the church too often feels like one more place of judgment.
blocks.es_reference: Justo después de un divorcio — cuando la vida se quiebra y la iglesia con demasiada frecuencia se siente como un lugar más de juicio.

blocks.en: Why people leave. Pastors like to believe the only reason for attending is devotion to Christ — but the truth is more human than that, and the repair of broken relationships must become a high priority for any church serious about retention. People leave when they move; when health fails in later years; when the church comes to feel irrelevant; when there is conflict with the pastor or other members; when work schedules or transportation or sheer busyness crowd the church out; when the preaching and teaching go dull — for if the sheep are not fed, they stop coming to the trough; and when marriages are strained, since the lower the marital satisfaction, the lower the church commitment tends to run. Mark especially the matter of conflict: in one study of dropouts, nearly a quarter had suffered some anxiety-provoking event, and not one of them was visited after they fell away. People give a church only a few weeks — six to eight — to notice they are gone. If no one reaches out in that window, they quietly reinvest their lives elsewhere.
blocks.es_reference: Por qué la gente se va. A los pastores les gusta creer que la única razón para asistir es la devoción a Cristo — pero la verdad es más humana que eso, y la reparación de relaciones rotas debe volverse una alta prioridad para toda iglesia seria en cuanto a la retención. La gente se va cuando se muda; cuando la salud falla en los años posteriores; cuando la iglesia llega a sentirse irrelevante; cuando hay conflicto con el pastor u otros miembros; cuando los horarios de trabajo o el transporte o el puro ajetreo desplazan a la iglesia; cuando la predicación y la enseñanza se vuelven aburridas — pues si las ovejas no son alimentadas, dejan de venir al comedero; y cuando los matrimonios están tensos, ya que cuanto más baja la satisfacción marital, más bajo tiende a correr el compromiso con la iglesia. Note especialmente el asunto del conflicto: en un estudio de desertores, casi una cuarta parte había sufrido algún evento que provoca ansiedad, y ni uno solo de ellos fue visitado después de apartarse. La gente da a una iglesia solo unas pocas semanas — seis a ocho — para notar que se han ido. Si nadie los alcanza en esa ventana, calladamente reinvierten su vida en otra parte.

blocks.en: Why people stay — and three ratios to build on. People remain where they are known and needed. Family and long membership ties hold them; so does genuine assimilation, which in close-knit settings happens naturally but in our mobile world must be planned. Three measurable ratios tell you whether the planning is working:
blocks.es_reference: Por qué la gente se queda — y tres proporciones sobre las cuales edificar. La gente permanece donde es conocida y necesitada. Los lazos de familia y de larga membresía la sostienen; también lo hace la asimilación genuina, que en entornos muy unidos ocurre con naturalidad pero en nuestro mundo móvil debe ser planeada. Tres proporciones medibles le dicen si la planeación está funcionando:

blocks.en: The friendship ratio, 7 to 1. A new member needs to make at least seven new friends in the church within his first six months. More is better; seven is the floor. Make fewer, and he will drift back to his old friends and his old life. People do not leave churches; they leave when they have no one in them.
blocks.es_reference: La proporción de amistad, 7 a 1. Un nuevo miembro necesita hacer al menos siete nuevos amigos en la iglesia dentro de sus primeros seis meses. Más es mejor; siete es el piso. Si hace menos, se alejará de vuelta a sus viejos amigos y su vieja vida. La gente no deja iglesias; se va cuando no tiene a nadie en ellas.

blocks.en: The role-and-task ratio, 60 to 100. For every hundred members there should be at least sixty meaningful roles and tasks — teacher, officer, committee member, singer, servant. New members especially need a real job, not busywork, so they can see where they fit and matter. A member with a task is a member with a reason to stay.
blocks.es_reference: La proporción de papeles y tareas, 60 por 100. Por cada cien miembros debería haber al menos sesenta papeles y tareas significativos — maestro, oficial, miembro de comité, cantante, servidor. Los nuevos miembros especialmente necesitan un trabajo real, no ocupaciones vacías, para que puedan ver dónde encajan e importan. Un miembro con una tarea es un miembro con una razón para quedarse.

blocks.en: The group ratio, 7 to 100. For every hundred members there should be at least seven groups. Groups create belonging, and they quietly drive the other two ratios — for it is in the group that friendships form and tasks are found.
blocks.es_reference: La proporción de grupos, 7 por 100. Por cada cien miembros debería haber al menos siete grupos. Los grupos crean pertenencia, y calladamente impulsan las otras dos proporciones — pues es en el grupo donde se forman las amistades y se hallan las tareas.

blocks.en:
Get those three right and you have not merely retained members; you
have woven them so thoroughly into the body that there is no loose
thread to pull.
blocks.es_reference: Acierte en esas tres y no habrá meramente retenido miembros; los habrá entretejido tan a fondo en el cuerpo que no queda hilo suelto que jalar.

blocks.en: Where We Are Now (2026)
blocks.es_reference: Dónde Estamos Ahora (2026)

blocks.en: Read this chapter today and it reads like prophecy. You wrote about the open back door of a single congregation; in the decades since, that back door has become the largest religious migration in the history of this country. The Great Dechurching we surveyed at the very beginning of this course — some forty million who once attended and no longer do — is nothing other than this unit’s problem written across a continent. And the cause the research now names is exactly the cause named here: most did not leave in a doctrinal crisis or a loss of faith. They drifted — they moved, life changed, a season ended — and no one reached for them in the six-to-eight-week window before they were gone. The four dropout seasons and the “nobody visited them” finding turn out to be the anatomy of the whole national exodus.
blocks.es_reference: Lea este capítulo hoy y se lee como profecía. Usted escribió sobre la puerta de atrás abierta de una sola congregación; en las décadas desde entonces, esa puerta de atrás se ha vuelto la migración religiosa más grande en la historia de este país. El Gran Abandono que examinamos al mismo principio de este curso — unos cuarenta millones que antes asistían y ya no — no es otra cosa que el problema de esta unidad escrito a lo ancho de un continente. Y la causa que la investigación ahora nombra es exactamente la causa nombrada aquí: la mayoría no se fue en una crisis doctrinal ni en una pérdida de fe. Se alejaron — se mudaron, la vida cambió, una temporada terminó — y nadie los alcanzó en la ventana de seis a ocho semanas antes de que se fueran. Las cuatro temporadas de deserción y el hallazgo de "nadie los visitó" resultan ser la anatomía de todo el éxodo nacional.

blocks.en: The years have added one trigger that could not have been foreseen in full, and it must be named. Beyond moving and busyness and dull preaching, a great many have been driven out by wounding — by conflict, yes, but also by the failures and scandals of leaders and by churches that proved unsafe. Some have walked through the long reexamination of faith now called deconstruction. The pastoral task this unit identified — the repair of broken relationships — is therefore larger and more urgent than ever, and it now includes humility about the church’s own sins and a door held genuinely open to those the church itself has hurt.
blocks.es_reference: Los años han añadido un detonante que no pudo preverse del todo, y debe nombrarse. Más allá de la mudanza y el ajetreo y la predicación aburrida, una gran cantidad ha sido expulsada por heridas — por conflicto, sí, pero también por las fallas y los escándalos de líderes y por iglesias que probaron ser inseguras. Algunos han pasado por el largo reexamen de la fe ahora llamado deconstrucción. La tarea pastoral que esta unidad identificó — la reparación de relaciones rotas — es por tanto más grande y más urgente que nunca, y ahora incluye humildad acerca de los propios pecados de la iglesia y una puerta sostenida genuinamente abierta a aquellos que la iglesia misma ha herido.

blocks.en: But here is the hope, and it is the right note to end the whole course on. That same back door swings both ways. The great company who left did not, for the most part, slam the door behind them — about half of them say they would consider coming back, and they are waiting, very often, for nothing more than an honest invitation and a real friend. Which means the three ratios are not merely a way to keep the people you have; they are now the strategy to win back the people you lost. The friend a returning believer needs is the seven-to-one friendship ratio. The place to belong is the seven-groups-per-hundred. The reason to stay is the role that says you are needed here. And the relentless contact we learned in the Sunday School unit — keep the name on the roll, reach for every soul — is simply the open back door watched from the inside.
blocks.es_reference: Pero aquí está la esperanza, y es la nota correcta para terminar todo el curso. Esa misma puerta de atrás se abre en ambos sentidos. La gran compañía que se fue no, en su mayor parte, dio un portazo al salir — cerca de la mitad de ellos dice que consideraría volver, y esperan, muy a menudo, nada más que una invitación honesta y un amigo real. Lo cual significa que las tres proporciones no son meramente una manera de conservar a la gente que tiene; son ahora la estrategia para recuperar a la gente que perdió. El amigo que un creyente que regresa necesita es la proporción de amistad de siete a uno. El lugar para pertenecer es el de siete grupos por cien. La razón para quedarse es el papel que dice se te necesita aquí. Y el contacto incansable que aprendimos en la unidad de la Escuela Dominical — conserve el nombre en la lista, alcance a cada alma — es sencillamente la puerta de atrás vigilada desde adentro.

blocks.en: So we end where the whole course has pointed. We have spoken of gathering, of forming, of keeping — front door, formation, back door. But all of it comes down to people, known and reached and loved into a body, and held there not by programs but by belonging. I will build my church, the Lord said, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. Our part is small and our part is glorious: to swing wide the front door, to form disciples within, and to stand at the back door with a hand outstretched — so that of all the Father gives us, by His grace, we lose none. The harvest is His. The growth is His. We are only, and gladly, the laborers in His field.
blocks.es_reference: Así que terminamos donde todo el curso ha apuntado. Hemos hablado de reunir, de formar, de conservar — puerta de entrada, formación, puerta de atrás. Pero todo se reduce a personas, conocidas y alcanzadas y amadas hasta entrar en un cuerpo, y sostenidas allí no por programas sino por la pertenencia. Edificaré mi iglesia, dijo el Señor, y las puertas del infierno no prevalecerán contra ella. Nuestra parte es pequeña y nuestra parte es gloriosa: abrir de par en par la puerta de entrada, formar discípulos dentro, y pararnos en la puerta de atrás con la mano extendida — para que de todo lo que el Padre nos da, por Su gracia, no perdamos a ninguno. La mies es Suya. El crecimiento es Suyo. Somos solo, y con gozo, los obreros en Su campo.

sa.prompt: Explain why retention matters as much as evangelism, using the leaking-bucket image.
sa.model: It is easier to keep a member than to win a new one, so retention matters as much as evangelism. A church that pours new members in the front while they leak out the back is a bucket with a hole; it can run the evangelism faucet at full force and the water level never rises. Closing the back door is as urgent as opening the front.

sa.prompt: Name and explain the high-risk 'dropout seasons' when people are most likely to leave a church.
sa.model: People leave most in predictable seasons: the teen years and young adulthood, the highest-risk span; the first two years in a new community before roots form; the stretch after the youngest child leaves home and the family's reason for attending seems to go; and the months just after a divorce. Each is a season of transition, exactly when the church must hold on tightest.

sa.prompt: Explain the critical first-weeks window. Why are the first six to eight weeks decisive for whether a newcomer stays?
sa.model: The first six to eight weeks are the decisive window; most who eventually drop out were never visited or connected in those first weeks. A newcomer who is welcomed, contacted, and folded in quickly forms the bonds that hold; one left alone quietly concludes he was not missed and slips away. Assimilation that does not happen early usually does not happen at all.

sa.prompt: Explain the friendship ratio and why friendships are the strongest cord holding a member.
sa.model: The friendship ratio holds that a new member needs to make about seven friends in the church within his first six months. Friendships are the strongest cord, because people stay where they are known and loved; a member with several real friends belongs and will weather offenses and dry seasons, while one who makes no friends has nothing personal holding him and soon drifts out.

sa.prompt: Explain the role/task ratio and the group ratio. How do tasks and groups hold a member?
sa.model: A healthy church needs roughly sixty roles or tasks per hundred members and about seven groups per hundred, so there is real work and a real circle for nearly everyone. A member with a task is needed and would be missed if absent; a member in a small group is known and carried. Tasks give a reason to belong and groups give a place to belong, and both hold a member in.

sa.prompt: List the common reasons people give for leaving a church. Which are about the church and which about life?
sa.model: Some reasons are about life: a move, failing health, a schedule or transport problem, the busyness that crowds church out. Others are about the church: conflict, a sense that the church became irrelevant, dull preaching, strain that follows them from a struggling marriage. Most are not dramatic crises of belief; people drift out the back for ordinary reasons, which is why ordinary care holds them in.

sa.prompt: Explain how the 'back door' has become the whole national dechurching, and what that reveals about how most people leave.
sa.model: The back door is no longer a trickle of individuals but the whole national dechurching, tens of millions slipped out the back over a generation. What it reveals is that most did not leave in a loud crisis of doctrine; they drifted quietly, unnoticed and unmissed, for ordinary reasons. The dechurching is mainly a back-door problem of people no one held onto, not a front-door problem of belief.

sa.prompt: What newer causes of leaving must we now add, and how do they differ from the ordinary drift?
sa.model: Beyond ordinary drift, we must now add wounding, scandal, and deconstruction. Some left because a leader's fall broke their trust; some were hurt by the church itself; some are reexamining an inherited faith and walking out in the process. These differ from quiet drift because they carry pain or doubt, so reaching them again calls not just for an invitation but for honesty, repentance, and the rebuilding of trust.

sa.prompt: Explain the hopeful truth that the back door 'swings both ways,' and what it asks of the church.
sa.model: The same back door people drift out of, they can also walk back through; about half of those who left say they would consider returning. So the back door swings both ways, and the great dechurching is also a great opportunity. It asks the church to go after the drifted with an honest, gracious invitation home, and to be the kind of community worth returning to.

sa.prompt: Synthesis: Show how the three ratios become a 're-churching' strategy, and tie it to Christ's promise to lose none.
sa.model: The three ratios, friends, roles, and groups, are a re-churching strategy: weave friendships, give every member a task, and fold everyone into a group, and people both stay and can be drawn back. Applied to the returning dechurched, the same cords that retain also reassimilate. This serves Christ's own promise over His people, that of those given to Him He would lose none; the church closes the back door because the Shepherd means to keep His sheep.
